name: Pendred syndrome
aliases: deafness with enlarged vestibular aqueduct and goitre

reference.source: Cummings Otolaryngology / Emery's Principles of Medical Genetics
clinicalPearls: Classic triad is sensorineural hearing loss, an enlarged vestibular aqueduct on imaging, and euthyroid goitre from an iodine organification defect
Caused by biallelic mutations in SLC26A4, which encodes the anion transporter pendrin; inheritance is autosomal recessive
Hearing loss is usually congenital or prelingual and may fluctuate or progress in a stepwise fashion, sometimes after minor head trauma
Enlarged vestibular aqueduct (with or without cochlear incomplete partition) is the most consistent temporal-bone finding on CT or MRI
Goitre often develops later, in later childhood or adolescence, and thyroid function is typically normal, so its absence does not exclude the diagnosis
A perchlorate discharge test can demonstrate the underlying iodine organification defect but is now largely superseded by genetic testing
Advise patients to avoid activities with head-injury risk that may precipitate sudden drops in hearing
reference.pathophysiology: Pendred syndrome results from loss-of-function mutations in SLC26A4, encoding pendrin, a transmembrane anion (chloride/iodide/bicarbonate) exchanger expressed in the inner ear, thyroid and kidney. In the inner ear, impaired pendrin function disturbs endolymph ion and pH homeostasis, contributing to abnormal cochlear and vestibular development, an enlarged vestibular aqueduct, and sensorineural hearing loss. In the thyroid, defective iodide transport into the follicular lumen impairs organification of iodine, producing goitre while thyroid hormone levels are often maintained. The same gene can also cause non-syndromic hearing loss with enlarged vestibular aqueduct when thyroid involvement is absent.
additionalDifferentials: Non-syndromic hearing loss with enlarged vestibular aqueduct (DFNB4)
Congenital hypothyroidism with dyshormonogenesis and goitre
Other syndromic sensorineural hearing loss such as Waardenburg or Usher
Acquired fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss from other causes
Isolated multinodular goitre unrelated to hearing loss
additionalInvestigations: Audiometry with serial testing to document fluctuating or progressive loss
High-resolution CT or MRI of the temporal bones for enlarged vestibular aqueduct and cochlear anomalies
Thyroid function tests and thyroid ultrasound to assess goitre
Perchlorate discharge test where genetic testing is unavailable
SLC26A4 molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
redFlags: Sudden or stepwise deterioration in hearing, especially after head trauma
Progressive goitre or evolving thyroid dysfunction requiring endocrine review
Vertigo or imbalance suggesting associated vestibular involvement
Bilateral profound loss threatening speech and language development in a child
reference.prognosis: Hearing loss tends to be progressive and may fluctuate, with many patients eventually developing severe-to-profound loss suited to hearing aids or cochlear implantation; the goitre is usually benign and euthyroid, though thyroid function should be monitored over time.
pitfalls: Excluding Pendred because goitre is absent in a young child before it typically develops
Overlooking an enlarged vestibular aqueduct on imaging as the key structural clue
Not warning patients about head-injury and pressure-related hearing drops
Assuming a euthyroid goitre is unrelated to the hearing loss
references: Cummings Otolaryngology: Head and Neck Surgery
Emery's Elements of Medical Genetics and Genomics
management: Manage sensorineural hearing loss with hearing aids and cochlear implantation for severe-to-profound loss
Provide early audiological rehabilitation with speech and language therapy and educational support for prelingual loss
Advise avoidance of head trauma and contact sports that may precipitate stepwise hearing deterioration in enlarged vestibular aqueduct
Monitor thyroid function and goitre size, and give thyroid hormone replacement if hypothyroidism develops
Perform serial audiometry to track fluctuating or progressive hearing loss
Refer for co-ordinated otology, audiology and endocrinology care
Offer genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive condition and screen affected siblings
